title: Stop re-reading your word list: test yourself instead | Words That Stick #2
description:
Re-reading your word list feels like studying. But it mostly trains you to recognise a word, not to find it when you need to speak.

The fix: cover the answer and make your brain find it.

Cover the word after each arrow and say it out loud:
• very angry → livid
• very busy → swamped
• very tired → exhausted
• very happy → thrilled
• very important → crucial

4 words for "very important", one picture each:
• crucial: the penalty kick that decides the match
• vital: the air in a diver's tank
• essential: your passport on a trip abroad
• urgent: a burst pipe you must fix right now

Try it tomorrow: cover the new words on your list, read the meaning, say the word, then check.

More words for "important": https://anotherwordfor.net/another-word-for-important/

Next episode: the best days to review a new word.

Source: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. (2006). Test-enhanced learning: Taking memory tests improves long-term retention. Psychological Science, 17(3), 249–255. One week later, students who practised recall remembered about 61% of a text; students who re-read it remembered about 40%, with the same study time.
